families.name: dark dot to blotch to spots
families.pattern: One small dark round mark on pale ground grows into scattered dark blotches, then into a spotted versus plain coat.
families.evidence: acts held at every step: s1:29->s2:71 drops 1.09; s2:71->s3:222 0.32/2.1 (controls ~0); s3:222->s4:35 2.30/22.7. A chain, not a split: each channel has one tested child here. s2:71 also feeds s3:134 (no card) and dog eyes use the same dot.

families.name: fan of thin lines to strand shape
families.pattern: Thin lines fanning from a centre split into three kinds of strand: hanging, curled, draped.
families.evidence: s2:112->s3:118 acts .67 (controls ~0); s3:118 -> 242/219/162 falls .82/.89/1.55 (controls ~0). Real one-parent, three-child split. s3:32 (ears) also feeds 242 (.64) and s3:125 pushes 242 DOWN, so 242 has opposing parents. Each drop is a small share of the firing.

families.name: ruled straight lines to bundles
families.pattern: Regular straight ruled lines build many parallel straight strands in a bundle versus a pebbly surface.
families.evidence: s3:240->s4:467 falls 1.56; s3:125->s4:467 .52 (controls ~0). s3:125 has the opposite sign on s4:242, so it cuts across the fan-of-lines family. Only one tested child.

families.name: whole-body tone
families.pattern: Which overall tone fills the body: pale, warm, or dark, as a split of one coat colour.
families.evidence: acts held: s3:186->28 2.70, ->31 3.54; s3:255->31 1.49; s3:90->172 1.73, ->42 .94; s3:254->172 1.59; s3:159->28 .90 (controls ~0). Two hubs (pale, warm) each with two children. s4:270 (white cloth) is probably a third child of s3:186 but was not tested.

families.name: face length
families.pattern: Narrow tapered face versus flat short face, built from a smooth narrow face without a ruff.
families.evidence: s3:141->s4:418 falls 6.61 (largest seen), s2:73->s3:141 .72 (controls ~0). s2:73 sheet never opened, so what it is is unknown.

families.name: body build: lean legs versus round bulk
families.pattern: Long lean legged body versus low round bulky or heavily furred body; the head version splits pointed from round.
families.evidence: s3:128->s4:9 falls 1.75/20.3 (held). s3:76->s4:156 .54/17.0 (weak). s2:6->s3:128 .12/3.6 and s2:6->s3:76 .38/3.3 are weak; one parent s2:6 of two siblings is suggested only.

families.name: plain ground beside an edge
families.pattern: A smooth plain field (sky, water, slope, colour patch) fills the frame beside or behind the subject, versus fine texture or close detail.
families.evidence: s2:120->s3:71 .38 (controls ~.005); s3:71->56 .28, ->163 3.36/13.5, ->277 .31 (held). s3:33->226 2.02 held, ->56 .39 held. s3:33 failed on s4:474 (0.00) and was noisy on s4:168, so it is a broad parent with uneven reach.

families.name: hard flat marks versus soft or limbed body
families.pattern: Hard printed marks on a flat surface versus a soft furry or limbed body.
families.evidence: s3:17->255 1.60/18.4; ->362 1.21/20.1 (controls ~.1). s3:17 also pushes s4:163 DOWN (weight -1.8), so one parent gives opposite signs to two children. s3:33->255 .86 held. s2:109->s3:17 failed (rose .08).

families.name: furry face as the turned-away pole
families.pattern: At stage 3 several channels differ in what they let through, but they share a furry eyed face on the negative side.
families.evidence: A shared negative pole read from sheets (neg), not from a parent. Tested links: s2:127->s3:164 .58/3.13, s2:109->s3:101 .35/2.89 (controls ~0). No stage 4 child tested, so this is a co-pole group, not a parent and children. s3:79 has the opposite sign. By the numbers no gate exists at stage 2.

families.name: thin edge on empty ground to spread shapes
families.pattern: A thin or spreading shape on bare ground versus round smooth closed shapes.
families.evidence: s3:158->168 1.55, ->431 .83, ->424 .51 (weak); s3:98->168 2.64 (controls .22). s4:182 untested (only top feeder number). 424 is a thick-hide channel so the pattern fits it loosely.

families.name: object entering a smooth empty field
families.pattern: A narrow or vivid object enters from the edge of a smooth empty field; one smooth sweep versus dense small parts.
families.evidence: acts: s3:59->32 .31, s3:99->32 .36, s3:103->32 .42 (controls ~0) of 15.9; s3:99->403 .59/17.4. s4:32 has three small parents, each 2-3% of peak. s3:59 also feeds s4:486 (see pointed shapes).

families.name: round bumps to clump
families.pattern: Small round blobs, alone or packed, build a dense clump of round bumps.
families.evidence: Both parents act about 1.2 of 18 on s4:400 (controls ~0). Two parents, one child.

families.name: pointed and tapered shapes
families.pattern: A narrow tapered or pointed shape (tip, ears, rigging) versus soft furry or closed shapes.

families.name: long straight edge to lattice
families.pattern: Long straight thin edges across plain ground build a criss-cross lattice.

families.name: hard parallel hardware versus spokes
families.pattern: Rows of small hard parallel parts versus thin spokes or wings on open ground.
families.evidence: s3:217->456 held (sheet checked); s3:191 .37 and s3:7 .41 held but sheets unclear; s2:32->s3:217 .168 weak. Fits train versus bike/plane split (score .91-.97 vs .36).

families.name: stage 1 to 2 stroke pairs
families.pattern: Stage 1 stroke dials combine into thin junction, disc or rim shapes in stage 2.
families.evidence: acts: s1:51->s2:59 .81, s1:43->s2:23 .51 (controls ~0); s1:60->s2:25 .169 (weak). Children of these s2 channels are mostly unread (s2:23 -> s3:60 only by trace).

families.name: stem-refinement dials
families.pattern: Each stage 1 channel is its same-number stem channel, sharpened as a dial on stroke size or shape.
families.evidence: Same-number stem channel gives 40-80% of the positive feed in every card. Not tested by acts. This is one-to-one copying, not branching.

shape: Not a clean tree. The tested links form a layered graph with strong edges: a stage 3 parent often has 2 to 3 children (s3:118, s3:186, s3:90, s3:71, s3:17, s3:158), but every stage 4 child has 2 to 4 parents, each worth 2 to 20% of its firing, and one parent gives opposite signs to two children (s3:17, s3:125). Chains are rare: only one runs stage 1 to 4 (dots to spots). Branching starts at stages 1 to 2 only as one-to-one copies. Evidence stops at the removal of single parents; unread parents hide most feed, and no s4 to logits link was used.
